newsitem.title: USA: NYS agency to sell new U.N. hotel bonds at closing.
newsitem.headline: NYS agency to sell new U.N. hotel bonds at closing.

text.p: A New York State agency, U.N. Development Corp, will defease $163 million of bonds for the U.N. Plaza Hotel and competitively sell $156 million just before the hotel sale closes, a city official said Tuesday.
"The last act of the closing is the bond issuing," said a spokesman for the New York City Economic Development Agency. "July 17 is the outside (closing) date," he added.

New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani and New York State Gov George Pataki said earlier that the city had agreed to sell the U.N. Plaza Hotel to Regal Hotels International Ltd for $102 million. This will be Regal Hotels first hotel in New York City.
Giuliani said the city expects the sale to produce $85 million for its 1998 fiscal year, which starts on June 30, once transaction fees and debt reduction costs are deducted.
The new bonds were attributed to the office part of the building, the spokesman for the Economic Development Corporation said, adding they will have the same 2026 maturity as the outstanding bonds.
About $7 million of the bonds that are linked to the hotel will be defeased.
The spokesman added the office building is more than capable of supporting the new debt, as it the coverage ratio is almost two times debt service.

By using the Economic Development Corporation, the city was able to sidestep requirements that it auction properties, a method that would not have proved as lucrative for the city, the spokesman said.

He explained that due to the deal's complexity, would-be buyers in an auction would have discounted the hotel's purchase price as they would have to negotiate sales documents--a process that took the city and Regal Hotels about one month.
